public_payload.normalized_proposition: Careless media coverage of data center deals is letting con artists get rich and setting up another great financial crisis.

statement.excerpt: The flippancy with which the media reports on these data centers — both in the structure of the deals and the realities of the construction (I go into detail about this in a premium from late last year, but making data centers is hard) — is allowing con artists to get rich and creating the conditions for yet another great financial crisis.
statement.document_title: Why Are We Still Doing This?

from_speaker: The flippancy with which the media reports on these data centers
is allowing con artists to get rich
creating the conditions for yet another great financial crisis
our_interpretation: Read this as a claim about a causal process already operating by the post date, not a prediction that a crisis must occur by an unstated deadline.
The ordinary test is whether misleading or materially incomplete coverage helped induce financing, enriched demonstrably deceptive promoters, and increased systemic financial vulnerability.
“Con artists” requires evidence of deception; risky investments or rising wealth alone do not establish it.
No numerical threshold for a great financial crisis or the media's contribution is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Credible evidence traces material omissions or misleading coverage to investor decisions, gains by deceptive promoters, and consequential systemic exposure.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible investigation of the implicated financing shows that the alleged deceptive enrichment or media-driven financing mechanism did not occur, or that the claimed systemic transmission mechanism was absent.
